newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Emperor says strikes gold in Fiji.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Emperor says strikes gold in Fiji.

text.p: Emperor Gold Mines Ltd said on Friday drill testing had revealed encouraging results at the Tuvatu prospect, 50 km south of the company's gold mine at Vatukoula in Fiji.
"Forty holes drilled in the Tuvatu area confirm beyond doubt there is a significant ore body," Emperor's chief executive officer, Collin Patterson, said in a statement.
Another 150 holes will now be drilled to confirm the size of the resource, he said.
Surface exploration has revealed gold mineralisation over 1,500 metres horizontally and around 300 metres vertically, ample to justify the additional drilling, he said.
One hole at Tuvatu intersected a mineralised zone of 109 metres at 4.8 grams of gold a tonne from 7.5 metres to 116.5 metres, downhole, Patterson said.

"This was an oblique intersection that included 3.3 metres at a spectacular 135.7 grams/tonne from 113.2 metres to 116.5 metres, and an unassayed zone of 33.2 metres that was assigned zero grade from 10.5 to 43.7 metres," he said.
Patterson said Emperor holds an option over the area known as Tuvatu, located in the west of Fiji's Viti Levu Island.
It produces 125,000 ounces a year from its underground mine at Vatukoula.
